caption:
Anthropic was expected to start its IPO roadshow next week and list in November.
After the worst tech selloff in a year, potential investors told Reuters they doubt that timeline and want a lower price.
The Wall Street Journal reported that some big investors see the valuation closer to $1 trillion than the $1.5 trillion that was discussed.

paragraphs.text: Potential investors in Anthropic's initial public offering are questioning whether the company can hold its planned roadshow the week of November 9 and still list in November, Reuters reported on November 5, 2026, citing four people familiar with the discussions. The roadshow had been expected to start that week, with pricing the following week.

The doubts followed a broad selloff in technology stocks. According to Yahoo Finance, the Nasdaq fell more than 5 percent on November 5, the S&P 500 dropped nearly 4 percent and the Dow fell more than 3 percent, with chip makers including AMD, Broadcom, Micron and Nvidia among the biggest decliners. PYMNTS, citing Reuters, said it was the Nasdaq's biggest one-day drop since April 2025.

Reuters reported that investors are pushing for a more attractive price. Some view the recently discussed valuation of $1.5 trillion as the high end of expectations, after earlier talk this year of seeking up to $2 trillion. Some people expect the offering itself to raise as much as $100 billion.

The Wall Street Journal reported that three major investors said Anthropic is unlikely to reach the $1.5 trillion figure, and one suggested a valuation nearer $1 trillion, according to a summary by PYMNTS. PYMNTS also reported that Anthropic executives and advisers were expected to meet within days.

Reuters said Anthropic may need to offer a larger discount to win commitments because of its record of quarterly losses and its large commitments to partners. Investing.com reported that the company's amended filing on November 2 showed third quarter revenue of about $16.96 billion and a net loss of about $23.29 billion, along with roughly $895.4 billion in purchase commitments and leases, mostly for computing power.

Investors are also waiting for October revenue figures, which Anthropic left blank in its updated filing, to see whether growth has recovered after a recent slowdown, according to Reuters. If AI stocks stay under pressure, the company could delay the listing until markets settle, possibly until the end of the year. Anthropic declined to comment to Reuters.

The selloff came after the US midterm elections on November 3, which gave Democrats control of the House and Senate, according to Yahoo Finance. Reuters said ballot measures limiting data center development in many states have added to political opposition to data centers and AI, a concern for companies that depend on building large computing sites.

Prediction markets moved quickly. Yahoo Finance reported that the odds on Kalshi that Anthropic goes public by November 30 fell from 84 percent to 60 percent during the day, while the odds for a listing by December 31 fell from 90 percent to 74 percent. Polymarket showed similar figures.

Nothing in the reporting says Anthropic has changed its plan, and a delay of a few weeks would not by itself change the company's business. The bigger question is price: a listing near $1 trillion instead of $1.5 trillion would reset expectations for every large AI company that hopes to go public, including OpenAI.
The clearest signal will be whether Anthropic starts its roadshow the week of November 9 as expected or announces a new schedule.
